_comment: PORT campaign: bridge 1 of IBM Spyre deeptools — SuperDSC -> DataflowIR.
The scope is ONE self-contained translation unit, cpp/bridge1.cpp, holding the 110 function
bodies to port, extracted verbatim from the authority tree and each preceded by a banner
giving its entry number and its ORIGINAL <file>:<line>.
There is no MLIR, LLVM or dcc header anywhere in this campaign. cpp/prelude.inc catalogues the
names the bodies reach so the unit stands alone; it carries names and shapes only — the
behaviour to port lives in the bodies.
_comment_scope: 106  dsc-based-utils/DSC2ToDataflowIR — THE conversion. Its header guard is literally
DSC2ToDataflowIR(SuperDsc*, MLIRContext&, bool uniformization, const DesignSpaceConfigGlobal&).
4  the DDL compiler's DERIVATIONS, which the conversion does NOT call — in the reference they
run before a SuperDsc exists, so a call graph rooted at the conversion is blind to them.
They are named explicitly because scratchy currently INVENTS them in
crates/compiler/deeptools/src/islands/.../shape.rs, and removing that is why this
checkConstraints            ddc/ddcv1.cpp:792   130L  — a LAMBDA nested in
checkConstraintsImpl (:825, 82L), so one unit covers both.
_comment_scope_correction: ⚠ A CORRECTION TO THE CAMPAIGN BRIEF, MEASURED. The brief lists getCumulativeStickSizes as
'verified present' in ddc/ddcv1.cpp at :789 and :1723. Those are CALL SITES on a `currDsc`
object. The DEFINITION is DesignSpaceConfig::getCumulativeStickSizes at dsc/dsc2.cpp:4109
(declared dsc/designSpaceConfig.h:260), and its body is a 6-line fold over getStickSizes —
so getStickSizes at dsc/dsc2.cpp:4066 carries the actual per-dim stick arithmetic and is in
scope with it. That is 2 units from `dsc/`, which the brief otherwise declares out of scope;
the rest of the 39,440-line dsc data model stays out.
Also measured: ddc/ddcv1.cpp holds 25 top-level definitions totalling 3,705 of its 3,818 lines,
and 21 named lambdas nested inside them. Only the 2 named above are in scope; the other 23
top-level functions are the DDL compiler's own allocation and scheduling passes, which run
before a SuperDsc exists and which scratchy does not reimplement.
_comment_excluded: 19 further inline definitions live in the conversion's headers and are NOT units, by the same
criterion bridge 2 used — what scratchy's architecture will never need, not what is unfinished:
16  1-3 line field accessors over a member (getCoreId, getUnitOp, getComponent, ...) — a
struct field in Rust, not a function.
table. In this crate a closed set is an enum and NEVER a string.
